meta.title: FORGE — Rugby Strength, Power & Conditioning Library
equipment_allowed: Bumper Plates / Lifting Platform (for Olympic-lift variants)

Novice.grip_work: Submaximal — build tissue tolerance, no max holds/carries to failure
Novice.conditioning_intensity: Zone 2, technical work-capacity blocks at 50-60% output
Novice.notes: Own the basic patterns (squat/hinge/press/pull/carry) and build tissue tolerance (neck, grip, low back) before any max-effort lifting or full-contact conditioning. No barbell work above 65% e1RM, no Olympic-lift variants yet, no heavy strongman implements (yoke/stones/log) — bodyweight-plus-light-load contact drills only.

Beginner.grip_work: Timed holds/carries submaximal (60-70% of max hold/carry time)
Beginner.conditioning_intensity: Zone 2-3, work blocks at 60-70% output, technical focus
Beginner.notes: Add posterior-chain, grip/neck and rotational-power volume. Light strongman implements (farmer's handles, light sandbag, light sled) enter the pool. Conditioning starts to take on match-shape (4-min blocks) rather than generic intervals.

Intermediate.grip_work: Max-effort timed holds/carries 1x/week, submaximal the rest
Intermediate.notes: Olympic-lift variants (hang clean/jerk/KB snatch) enter the pool for hip-power transfer to tackling/acceleration/lineout drive. Contrast method (heavy lift + explosive movement) becomes the main power tool. Full strongman implements (yoke, atlas stones, log press, tire flip) now programmed at moderate loads.

Advanced.grip_work: Max hangs/holds/carries programmed and tracked like a main lift
Advanced.conditioning_intensity: Zone 4-5, match-pace intervals at 85-95% output, sport-specific work-capacity blocks
Advanced.notes: Full season periodization (pre-season GPP -> SPP -> in-season maintenance -> playoff peak). Heavy strength/power sessions kept 48-72h from full-contact training or a match. Conditioning volume matches actual match minutes and interchange role.

Elite.training_age: 6+ years, competing at senior representative/professional level
Elite.intensity_main: 85-97% e1RM, RPE 8-10 only in peak block
Elite.intensity_power: Max intent, autoregulated by bar speed
Elite.grip_work: Fully individualized off actual scrum/tackle/carry fatigue data from training and GPS load
Elite.conditioning_intensity: Match-simulation pace, opponent/positional-role-modeled work:rest, GPS/HRV-guided intensity
Elite.notes: S&C fully subordinate to the fixture calendar, built backward from match day. Load is set by daily readiness/GPS data, not the written number — the written plan is a default the coach is expected to override.

match_format_reference.Age-Grade / School: 2 x 25-30 min halves, reduced or no contested scrum/contact depending on age grade
match_format_reference.Club (Senior Amateur): 2 x 40 min halves, full contact, standard interchange bench
match_format_reference.Professional: 2 x 40 min halves, full contact, expanded interchange (up to 8 replacements) and GPS-tracked high-speed running volume

global_rules: Every session follows this order: explosive/power work first -> main strength lift -> posterior-chain/accessory -> grip/neck/carry work last -> conditioning only on a day NOT preceded by a heavy strength or full-contact session.

Rugby loads both the strength system (scrum, maul, contact, lineout lift) and the running system (repeated high-speed efforts) in the same week — choose ONE positional emphasis per training block based on the athlete's actual playing group (Forwards / Backs) rather than trying to develop all qualities equally; Balanced (Utility) is the correct DEFAULT for pre-season, off-contract, or utility players who cover both.
Olympic-lift variants (hang clean/jerk/KB snatch) are Intermediate-level-and-up only — Novice/Beginner train the same power quality through trap-bar jumps, KB swings, and med-ball throws.

Strongman implements (yoke, atlas stones, log press, sandbag, tire flip, sledgehammer) are the primary tools for scrum/maul/tackle-specific contact strength. Light implements only from Beginner; full max-effort strongman work is Intermediate-level-and-up.
Reverse Hyper / GHD doubles as a posterior-chain builder (loaded, strength days) and a spinal-decompression recovery tool (bodyweight, high reps, day after a match or heavy contact session).

Heavy squat/hinge/pull sessions are placed 48h+ from full-contact training or a match wherever the weekly schedule allows — this is the first thing to protect when the fixture list gets congested (typical week: match Saturday, heavy lower body Monday/Tuesday, light/speed Thursday).
Deload every 4th week at 40-50% volume reduction for Intermediate and above in pre-season blocks; in-season volume is auto-reduced further by match load and travel.
Match week: heavy strength work stops 3 days out; only light power/speed touches (short accelerations, low-volume trap-bar jumps) remain up to the day before the match, then full rest and recovery.
